programme.title: Voyages of Discovery
programme.desc: Paul Rose tells the story of Captain James Cook's historic 1768 voyage to observe the transit of Venus, while also searching for a vast southern continent. No such land mass was discovered, but the crew of the Endeavour went on to Tahiti and Australia, which Cook claimed for Britain. The ship was almost ripped apart on the Great Barrier Reef, but the captain's navigational skills eventually steered it back home to safety

programme.title: This World
programme.sub-title: The Tea Trail with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: In the first of two This World documentaries examining the stories behind the nation's favourite beverages, adventurer and broadcaster Simon Reeve looks at the production of tea. He begins in the Kenyan coastal city of Mombasa, where most of the leaves for teabags are bought at auction, before travelling through eastern Africa to meet some of the millions of people who pick, pack and transport it. He drinks tea with everyone from Maasai cattle herders to the descendants of the original plantation owners, and hears claims of low wages and child labour

programme.title: Andy Warhol's America
programme.desc: A look at the artist's response to the Civil Rights movement and the assassination of John F. Kennedy, as well as other major historical events happening in America during the 1960s. Plus, stories about Warhol setting up the Silver Factory and managing the Velvet Underground, and also how he faced his own personal nightmare - he was shot by a Factory associate

programme.title: American Visions
programme.desc: Robert Hughes continues his journey through the American art world, stopping off to examine the revolutionary styles of the 1950s and 1960s. As the USA became a global superpower, consumer culture and Cold War paranoia grew, spawning a new generation of artists. The Abstract Expressionists, including Jackson Pollock, Willem de Kooning and Mark Rothko, believed the process of creating a painting as important as the finished product, while Andy Warhol and the Pop Artists celebrated the aesthetic qualities of everyday products.

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Mexico v England (Kick-off 1.00am). Coverage of the fourth round-of-16 match, which takes place at Mexico City Stadium. The co-hosts beat Ecuador 2-0 in the last round, thanks to first-half goals from Julian Quinones and Raul Jimenez, and have to concede in the tournament so far. Facing the Mexicans at this venue is a particularly tough test, as they have such an excellent record here over the years, and England undoubtedly need to improve if they are to progress to the quarter-finals, having scraped past DR Congo 2-1 in the previous round thanks to two goals by Harry Kane

programme.title: Wimbledon 2026
programme.desc: Clare Balding presents continued coverage of day seven of the Grand Slam event from the All England Club, featuring fourth-round matches in the men's and ladies' singles competitions. This day was traditionally a rest day at SW19, but that was changed in 2022, with one of the main reasons being that advances in grass technology and maintenance meaning the courts no longer required a day of recovery mid-tournament. The crowd were treated to a strong performance by Carlos Alcaraz against a competitive opponent on the seventh day last year, with the 2023 and 2024 champion defeating Andrey Rublev 6-7, 6-3, 6-4, 6-4. However, the Spaniard will not be present this year due to a wrist injury, leaving the likes of Rublev with possibly their best chance yet of winning a Grand Slam

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Portugal v Spain (Kick-off 8.00pm). Coverage of the fifth round-of-16 match, which takes place at Dallas Stadium in the USA. Portugal finished second in their group, below Colombia and above DR Congo and Uzbekistan with two draws and a win before coming back from behind in their round-of-32 match with Croatia to prevail 2-1. Spain got off to a disappointing start with a goalless draw against Cape Verde, but they are still yet to concede in this tournament, having followed that result up with wins against Saudi Arabia and Uruguay in the group stage, before comfortably defeating Austria 3-0 in the next round. However, this is likely to be their toughest test so far, and the last meeting between the Iberian rivals saw Portugal win on penalties after a 2-2 draw in the final of the 2024/25 UEFA Nations League in Germany

programme.title: Fuascail
programme.desc: A creative contemplation by visual artist, musician and composer Barry Kerr, known as Fuascail. Kerr uses a combination of his musical compositions and visual artistry to portray an abstract reflection on the revolutionary period of Ireland's history. Fuascail could by translated as release, redeem or resolve and Kerr uses these three pillars to tease out his own feelings around history, conflict and commemoration. The film is set in Connemara where Kerr spent much time drawing inspiration from the landscape and its history, composing new music and painting new work

programme.title: Motorhoming with Merton & Webster

The next day they visit the the Rollright Stones, where they meet Sharp and Blunt, an all-female morris dancing group from nearby Adderbury.

programme.desc: Paul and Bob take a sleeper train to the Scottish Highlands on a quest for ferox trout. Having fished long and hard, the pair take a bit of time out to look for another, more elusive local quarry - the Loch Ness Monster

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob set off in a punt to fish for perch on a weir pool on the River Thames, leaving poor old terrier Ted forlorn on the river bank as he is not allowed on the boat with them. After a tiring morning, they decide to fish an altogether quieter spot and sit on the bankside discussing their guilty pleasures in music. They also chat to author and comic, Richard Herring, who discusses his battle with testicular cancer

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing

Plus, Dr Anand Patel, an expert in men's health, joins Bob for a chat about weight

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing

They head out on boats and try out a new technique called dapping, with local guide Richie Johnston providing much-needed assistance, and also helping them in their quest to find out what exactly the 'craic' is, where to find it and how to experience it

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul head off for a festive fishing trip to Norway, travelling to Vesteralen and the Lofoten Islands in the Arctic Circle and face a mighty maelstrom. The chain of islands is 1,000 miles north of Oslo and made up of majestic mountains, deep fjords and long, surf-swept beaches, and the pair are on a mission to find a variety of species including cod, halibut and pollock, and the ultimate prize, the hard-fighting coalfish. Along the way Bob surprises Paul with some unique accommodation in the most remote locations they have ever experienced, and the pair enjoy an array of culinary festive delights, including Christmas porridge and traditional Christmas cookies. programme.desc: Paul Merton and Suki Webster take to the roads again, beginning by heading to Cornwall, home to crystal-clear waters, picturesque fishing villages and beautiful beaches. Their first destination is the Lizard - the most southerly point on the British mainland - where they go seal watching, before going out with a local fisherman to try their hands at catching spider crabs

programme.title: Motorhoming with Merton & Webster
programme.desc: Paul Merton and Suki Webster explore the Cotswolds, helping Richard and his apprentice Innis build a dry stone wall before driving to their first off-grid campsite, pitching up for the night for an al fresco three-course dinner. The next day they visit the the Rollright Stones, where they meet Sharp and Blunt, an all-female morris dancing group from nearby Adderbury.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob take a sleeper train to the Scottish Highlands on a quest for ferox trout. It's a tall order for any angler but they have a local guide to help them along the River Garry. Having fished long and hard, the pair take a bit of time out to look for another, more elusive local quarry - the Loch Ness Monster

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob set off in a punt to fish for perch on a weir pool on the River Thames, leaving poor old terrier Ted forlorn on the river bank as he is not allowed on the boat with them. After a tiring morning, they decide to fish an altogether quieter spot and sit on the bankside discussing their guilty pleasures in music. They also chat to author and comic, Richard Herring, who discusses his battle with testicular cancer

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob head to a lake deep in the Surrey Hills, an area of outstanding natural beauty. As they approach the gates to the lake, they set their eyes and their hearts on catching big carp from the yet undisturbed and tranquil waters. Plus, Dr Anand Patel, an expert in men's health, joins Bob for a chat about weight

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob venture to the west of Ireland to fish the mighty Lough Corrib, regarded as one of the best places in the country to try trout fishing. They head out on boats and try out a new technique called dapping, with local guide Richie Johnston providing much-needed assistance, and also helping them in their quest to find out what exactly the 'craic' is, where to find it and how to experience it

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul head off for a festive fishing trip to Norway, travelling to Vesteralen and the Lofoten Islands in the Arctic Circle and face a mighty maelstrom. The chain of islands is 1,000 miles north of Oslo and made up of majestic mountains, deep fjords and long, surf-swept beaches, and the pair are on a mission to find a variety of species including cod, halibut and pollock, and the ultimate prize, the hard-fighting coalfish. Along the way Bob surprises Paul with some unique accommodation in the most remote locations they have ever experienced, and the pair enjoy an array of culinary festive delights, including Christmas porridge and traditional Christmas cookies. Later, the duo are joined by Ulrika Jonsson to reminisce about their own very different and personal traditions of Christmas, and Freddie Flintoff presents the hotly contested Employee of the Year and Catch of the Year awards
